errors.english: by being skilled at distributing a considerable amount of meaningless things
errors.why: don ma yin pa is harm (anartha): the misdeeds are ones adept at bestowing no small harm, not a skill at distributing meaningless things.

fix.find: thereby accumulating uncommon misdeeds by being skilled at distributing a considerable amount of meaningless things,
fix.replace: thereby accumulating uncommon misdeeds adept at bestowing no small harm,

errors.english: is seen by those of equal or superior capability to be ineffective on the other side
errors.why: The verse says one should look at powerful rivals who are equal or superior, so pride born of sovereignty does not stay in the hearts of the good; the English makes those rivals the ones who see, and invents 'ineffective on the other side'.

note: Generally follows the commentary and its two exempla, but garbles the opening sentence about accumulating harmful misdeeds and the Catuḥśataka verse on pride.

errors.english: transforming the mental continuum [note: original: "rgyud," referring to the stream of consciousness]
errors.why: The continuum being transformed is the series of the mantra itself (santāna-pariṇāma of the mantra), not a person's mental stream.

note: A sound rendering of the argument against the Mīmāṃsā view of mantra efficacy; only the note on rgyud misleads.

errors.english: The actual engagement of the mind with an existing entity, by producing a cause characterized by a conflicting habitual tendency, causes the mind that grasps non-existence to sever the continuity.
errors.why: It is the cognition of non-existence that cuts off the continuity of the cognition of an entity by producing a contrary cause (a vāsanā); the English makes the entity-cognition the producer.

errors.english: just as coldness is produced by fire
errors.why: The Tibetan cites fire and cold, the standard example of non-coexistence (cold removed by fire); nothing says fire produces cold.

note: The difficult argument on contradiction between conceptions is mostly followed, with two slips in who acts on what.

errors.english: That [note: the ultimate nature] is not of the same category as those [note: ordinary perceptions]. If you ask who possesses those perceptions:
errors.why: The root verse says this is not fit for (knowing) reality, and the commentary asks 'by whom?'; the commentary's own later paraphrase says 'not fit for that reality'.

fix.find: That [note: the ultimate nature] is not of the same category as those [note: ordinary perceptions]. If you ask who possesses those perceptions: it is all those who do not see the supreme.
fix.replace: That is not fit for reality. By whom, you ask? By all those who do not see the supreme.

errors.english: regarding the meaning of reality which possesses equanimity [note: original: "upeksha"], characterized as being free from definitions: those who are the Buddhas
errors.why: The 'indifferent ones' are the Buddhas, who treat the reality-object (free of characteristics) with indifference; reality does not possess equanimity.

fix.find: regarding the meaning of reality which possesses equanimity [note: original: "upeksha"], characterized as being free from definitions: those who are the Buddhas
fix.replace: those who are indifferent [note: original: "upeksha"] toward the object of reality, which is free from characteristics, namely the Buddhas

note: The argument on duality and seeing reality is mostly right, but the root-verse line and the Buddhas' indifference to reality are misconstrued.

errors.english: if the person being carried is standing on land included within the border but has no such purpose [note: of evasion], there is no downfall. If the person being carried is on land included within the border [note: with intent], it is indeed a grave offense.
errors.why: khyer ba po is the carrier: no offense when the power does not need a carrier standing on land inside the boundary, and a sthūlātyaya when there is such a carrier; the notes about intent are invented.

fix.find: if the person being carried is standing on land included within the border but has no such purpose [note: of evasion], there is no downfall. If the person being carried is on land included within the border [note: with intent], it is indeed a grave offense.
fix.replace: where it needs no carrier standing on land included within the border, there is no downfall. Where the carrier stands on land included within the border, it is indeed a grave offense.

errors.english: and the value exceeds five (mashaka) small coins or similar measures, it is a grave offense
errors.why: The point is that even when the object reaches the full five māṣakas, it is only a sthūlātyaya; 'even' (yang) is lost and 'exceeds' replaces 'amounts to'.

note: The Vinaya rules on hamstringing and evading tolls through the air are rendered adequately, but the final ruling on carriers is misattributed.

errors.why: The label refers back to the preceding verses ('If words engaged only the ultimate...'), which are themselves given as prose; the English turns it into a heading for the following prose argument.

fix.replace: [The preceding lines] are the summary verses.

errors.english: regarding the entities dwelling in that subject, one ponders
errors.why: It is those who take that subject as their topic (the disputants) who consider whether the object has a real material cause; they are not entities dwelling in the subject.

note: The apoha argument is mostly tracked, but the summary verses are run into prose and their label is attached to the wrong passage.

errors.english: refers to the position of we.
errors.why: pha rol gyi'o says this phrase is the opponent's, not 'ours'.

fix.find: refers to the position of we.

errors.why: In context, paired with mind and mental factors, this is the elements and what derives from the elements (bhūta/bhautika), not 'arising and not arising'.

errors.english: the mutual relationship between feelings like pleasure and other sentient factors
errors.why: sems pa can is the Sāṃkhya conscious principle (puruṣa/cetana), set against pleasure etc. (the guṇas), not 'other sentient factors'.

errors.english: consciousness appears as distinct substances of mutually different aspects
errors.why: Substances of mutually different aspect appear separately to cognition; consciousness does not appear as the substances.

note: Follows the commentary's sequence of glosses, but misreads the Sāṃkhya terms and reverses whose position one phrase states.

errors.english: one should state "only existing in the pervader."
errors.why: The restriction is that in it (the reason) the pervader is only present; the English inverts the locus.

note: A careful, literal rendering of a dense passage on pakṣadharma and vyāpti; one restriction formula is inverted.

errors.why: skyes here is 'a gift': his words become like a gift when he meets the noble.

fix.find: when he meets with noble people, become manifest
fix.replace: when he meets with noble people, become like a gift

errors.english: being faultless in his limbs, he is able
errors.why: The faultless limbs are those of the speech (its members), which accomplishes the aim, not the speaker's bodily limbs.

note: The grammatical glosses on the verse are rendered faithfully, though tautologically; the key simile 'like a gift' is lost.
A faithful rendering of the passage on observation, non-observation, and substance versus quality.
